questions.question: The Constitution of India is a sovereign socialist secular democratic republic with a _________ system of government.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Parliamentary**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Parliamentary system**

 
 
• The **Constitution of India** is a sovereign socialist secular democratic republic with a **parliamentary system of government**.
 
• **India **has a parliamentary system of **government **with federal and unitary components.
 
• It is a sovereign** socialist, secular, **and **democratic** **republic**.
 
• The **Prime Minister** serves as the head of the **Council of Ministers**, which provides advice to the **President**, who is the nation's constitutional leader.
 
• The** Indian Constitution**, which was approved by the Constituent Assembly on** November 26, 1949**, and took effect on **January 26, 1950**, governs the **Country**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **​**The **head **of state in a **parliamentary system **is often a different person from the head of **government**. In contrast, in a presidential system, the executive branch does not receive its democratic legitimacy from the legislative and the head of state frequently doubles as the head of **government**.
 
• A **parliamentary** **system**, sometimes known as a parliamentarian democracy, is a form of democratic government in which the executive branch obtains the backing of the legislative, usually a **parliament**, to whom it is answerable.

questions.question: Which nutrient is chlorella rich in?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Protein**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__ **

__
 
• Chlorella__

 __
 
• Chlorella (green algae) is known as the Space algae and is used in space research.
 
• It serves as a good source of food for humans in space as it contains a high level of iron, vitamins and amino acids.
 
• It grows easily in the presence of sunlight, minerals and water and using hydroponics.
 
 
 
• **Protein**
 
 
• Although **protein** is a necessary macronutrient, not all protein-rich foods are made **equal**, and you may not require as much as you might believe.
 
• Discover the **fundamentals **of **protein** and how to incorporate** wholesome protein** meals into your **diet**.
 
• The body is made up of **protein**, which may be found in almost every **organ**, **tissue**, and** body part**, including **muscle**, **bone**, **skin**, and **hair**.
 
• It contributes to the **production **of **haemoglobin**, which transports **oxygen **in the **blood**, and **enzymes**, which drive numerous** chemical reactions**. You are made up of at least **10,000 distinct proteins**, which also keep you that way.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Amino acids** are the more than **twenty fundamental building components **used to make **protein**.
 
• Since we cannot store **amino acids**, our systems must either create them from **scratch **or **alter **existing ones.
 
• Nine **amino acids**, known as the essential amino acids, must be obtained from **food**: **histidine**, **isoleucine**, **leucine**, **lysine**, **methionine**, **phenylalanine**, **threonine**, **tryptophan**, and **valine**.

questions.question: Droupadi Murmu was elected the _______ President of India.
questions.solution:

__
 
• **Droupadi Murmu **

 
 
• **​Droupadi Murmu **was elected the **15****th** President of India.
 
• Since** July 25, 2022**, **Droupadi Murmu**, also known as **Puti Biranchi Tudu**, has held the office of India's **15th** president.
 
• She was born on** June 20, 1958**. After **Pratibha Patil**, she is the second woman to hold the position and the first member of a tribal community to do so.

• Her father and grandfather served as the local council's traditional leaders, or **Sarpanch **(Gram Panchayat).
 
• They gave her the name** Puti Tudu**.
 
• Her teacher changed her name from** Durpadi to Droupadi**, and she had previously gone by the names **Dorpdi **and **Durpadi**.

questions.question: What is the commercial unit of electric energy?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kilowatt hour**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kilowatt hour**

 
 
• ** Kilowatt hour** is the commercial unit of **electric energy.**
 
• **kWh **is a common unit of **electrical energy** (kilowatt-hour). It is defined as the amount of **energy **utilised for an hour by a **1kW **appliance.
 
• The** kilowatt-hour **(abbreviated kWh) is a unit of **energy** that represents the **energy **used to generate one **kilowatt **of **power **for one hour.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Although it is not a formal standard unit in any system, the** kilowatt-hour** is frequently employed in ele**ctrical applications**. The unit of electrical energy is the **kWh**, which is the same for **household **and **commercial use**.
 
• **Commercial units** are charged at a separate rate than household units, which is higher. It is mostly used to reduce power usage in factories and other commercial settings.

questions.question: In early 1610, who discovered with his newly invented telescope that Jupiter has four moons?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Galileo Galilei**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ** Galileo Galilei**

 
 
• **​Galileo di Vincenzo Bonaiuti de' Galilei**, frequently referred to as a **polymath**, was an **Italian** **astronomer**, **physicist**, and **engineer** who lived from **15 February 1564** to** 8 January 1642**.
 
• He was born in **Pisa**, which at the time belonged to the **Duchy of Florenc**e.
 
• **Galileo** has been referred to as the **"father" of modern science**, the scientific method, observational **astronomy**, and modern **physics**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Galileo **engaged on practical **science **and **technology**, detailing the characteristics of **pendulums** and** "hydrostatic balances," **
 
• He developed the thermoscope, created several military compasses, and made use of the telescope to make studies of celestial objects for science.
 
• Telescopic confirmation of Venus' phases, observations of Jupiter's four largest **satellites**, observations of **Saturn's rings**, and analyses of **lunar craters **and **sunspots** are only a few of his contributions to observational **astronomy**.

questions.question: By which name is the birthday of Lord Krishna famous?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Janmashtami**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Janmashtami**

 
 
• **​T**he birthday o**f Lord Krishna** famous is famous by the name of **Janmashtami**.
 
• **Krishna Janmashtami**, which translates to **"Occasion of the birth of Krishna,"** is a **Hindu festival** that honours the birth of **Krishna**, the **eighth **manifestation of **Vishnu**.
 
• It is also known as **Krishnashtami**, **Janmashtami**, or **Gokulashtami**. **Ashtami**, the eighth tithi of the **Krishna Paksha **(dark fortnight) of **Shraavana Masa** (according to amanta tradition) or **Bhadrapada Masa**, is the day on which it is observed in accordance with the **Hindu **lunisolar calendar (according to the purnimanta tradition).
 
• This falls during the **Gregorian calendar **months of **August** or **September**. 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Particularly in the Hindu **Vaishnavism **tradition, it is a significant **festival**.
 
• The celebrations of **Janmashtami **include **fasting **(upavasa), a **night vigil** (Ratri Jagaran), devotional **singing** through the midnight when **Krishna **was **born**,** dance-drama** reenactments of Krishna's life as described in the **Bhagavata Purana**.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a goal for the Green Revolution?

options.text: Rise in production of food grains

questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Expansion of Irrigation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Green Revolution**

 
 
• **​**The **Third Agricultural Revolution**, commonly known as the **Green Revolution**, was a time of technological transfer activities that resulted in significantly **higher crop yields** and **agricultural **output.
 
• Following **World War II**, these **agricultural **improvements started in industrialised **nations **and spread until the late **1980s**.
 
• Farmers started implementing new technologies in the late **1960s**, including **high-yielding cereal varieties**, particularly **dwarf wheat **and **rice**, and the widespread use of **chemical fertilisers**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Moreover, **mechanisation** and other more modern **cultivating** **techniques** were adopted in **agriculture**. These adjustments were frequently made as part of a set of procedures designed to replace older **agricultural technology**.
 
• These more expensive **technologies **were frequently offered alongside **loans **that were subject to the **developing countries** adopting new **policies**, like **privatising fertiliser production **and **distribution**, which was previously carried out through **public channels**.

questions.question: Which of the following metals was used to make weapons and tools in Harappan cities?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Copper**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Copper:**

 
 
• ​A number of copper tools and weapons have also been discovered.
 
• The common tools included an axe, saws, chisels, knives, spearheads and arrowheads. 
 
• Copper was brought mainly from Khetri in Rajasthan.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• The Indus Valley Civilization flourished between 2500 BC and 1750 BC.
 
• Harappa is a site in eastern Punjab province.
 
• Harappa was located on the banks of the river Ravi.
 
• Most Harappan sites are located in semi-arid lands, where irrigation was probably required for agriculture.
 
• Harappa was discovered by archaeologist Daya Ram Sahni.__
 
• He supervised the excavation of the Indus valley site at Harappa in 1921 and 1922.
 
• Harappa site was again excavated by Madho Swaroop Vatsa in 1926 and Wheeler in 1946.
 
• The major findings of Daya Ram Sahni from the Harappan site are:
 
 
• Sandstone statues of Human anatomy
 
• Granaries
 
• Bullock carts.
 
• Clay figures of Mother Goddess.
 
• Copper made mirror.
 
 
 
• Harappa was excavated by Mohammed Rafique Mughal of the Archaeological Survey of Pakistan in 1966 after independence.
 
• The Harappan city was heavily damaged under British rule when bricks from the ruins were used as track ballast in the construction of the Lahore–Multan Railway.

questions.question: The executive power of the Union is vested in the_________.

options.text: Council of Ministers headed by the Prime Minister
Chief Justice of the Supreme Court

questions.solution:
The correct answer is President.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The** President of India is the country's official head of state.​**
 
• According to** Article 53 (1) of the constitution, **the **President of India** has the majority of the **executive power.**
 
• According to the **aforementioned Article 53**, the President has the entire constitutional authority and may wield it either directly or through officials who report to him (1).
 
• According to the Constitution, the **President is the recognised leader of the Union's Executive.**
 
• The President and the two Houses known as the Rajya Sabha and the People's House make up the Council of the Parliament of the Union, under Article 79 of the Indian Constitution (Lok Sabha).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Council of Ministers headed by the Prime Minister**

 
 
• **The Union Council of Ministers**, which serves as the **top executive branch decision-making body**, is the **Government of India's main executive organ.**
 
• It is chaired by the prime minister and includes the **heads of all executive government ministries.**
 
 
 
• **Prime Minister**
 
 
• The **prime minister is the title given to the head of state in India.** The prime minister and their chosen **Council of Ministers have executive authority, **despite the fact that the president of India is the body's recognized head of state.
 
• The prime minister is frequently the leader of the party or coalition that holds a majority in the **Lok Sabha,** which serves as the **Republic of India's primary legislative body**
 
 
 
• **​Chief Justice of the Supreme Court**
 
 
• The Chief Justice is the head of the Supreme Court of India and the highest-ranking judge in the Indian judiciary.
 
• The Chief Justice is appointed by the President of India, after consultation with other senior judges of the Supreme Court.
 
• The Chief Justice typically serves until they reach the age of 65.

questions.question: Vempati Chinna Satyam was awarded the Padma Bhushan in 1998. He was a _______ dancer.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Kuchipudi.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Vempati Chinna Satyam, who lived from 15 October 1929 to 29 July 2012, was a legend in the Kuchipudi dancing style.**
 
• He is credited with spreading the dancing style's popularity all over the world.
 
• He has received numerous honours, including the **Raja Lakshmi Award from Madras and the Sangeet Peeth of Bombay.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** Kathak Dance**

 
 
• **One of the primary categories of ancient Indian classical dance, known as Kathak**, is thought to have started with the **wandering storytellers known as Kathakars in North India.**
 
• Similar to the early Greek theatre, these wandering **Kathakars **used music, dance, and songs to convey legendary tales.
 
• The** Bhakti movement**, a tendency of theistic devotion that emerged in **mediaeval Hinduism,** is when the genre first came into being.
 
 
 
• **Manipuri Dance**
 
 
• **Manipuri dance is one of India's most well-known classical dance** genres and is particularly renowned for its Vaishnavist themes and spectacular performances of **dance dramas centred on the love between Radha and Krishna known as "Ras Lila."**
 
• Additional subjects in this kind of art related to **Shaktism, Shaivism**, and the **sylvan gods known as Umang Lai during the Manipuri festival "Lai Haraoba."**
 
• Although this dance style has its roots in the **ancient Sanskrit Hindu literature "Natya Shastra," **it is named after the north-eastern Indian state of Manipur, where it first appeared.
 
 
 
• **Kathakali Dance**
 
 
• **An essential subgenre of Indian classical dance known as "Kathakali" **is linked to this **kind of storytelling.**
 
• It is a dance drama from Kerala in southern India. Like other **Indian traditional dance forms, "Kathakali"** uses spectacular facial and hand movements along with music and vocal performance to effectively convey the story to the audience.

questions.question: ‘Do or die’ slogan is given by which of the following freedom fighter?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Mahatma Gandhi.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mahatma Gandhi is associated with the maxim "do or die."**
 
• **During the Gandhiji-led Quit India Campaign, **this catchphrase was created.
 
• On August 9, 1942, **the Indian National Congress (INC),** under the direction of **Mahatma Gandhi**, formally introduced the catchphrase.
 
• **Its catchphrases were "Quit India" and "Bharat Chodo."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** Bal Gangadhar Tilak**

 
 
• **​At Ratnagiri, Maharashtra, on July 23, 1856, Bal Gangadhar Tilak was born.**
 
• **Bal Gangadhar Tilak, a lawyer and freedom fighter**, is also known by the name** Lokmanya Tilak**.
 
• **"Swaraj is my birthright, and I shall have it," is the slogan.**
 
 
 
• **Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel**
 
 
• **First Deputy Prime Minister and Home Minister of India from 1947 to 1950**, **Vallabhbhai Jhaverbhai Pate**l (31 October 1875 – 15 December 1950), also known as **Sardar Patel**, was an Indian lawyer, prominent political leader, barrister, and statesman.
 
• He was a lawyer and a prominent member of the **Indian National Congress **who** led the country's independence movement **and oversaw its fusion into a single, sovereign state.
 
 
 
• **Motilal Nehru**
 
 
• **Motilal Nehru**, a member of the **Indian National Congress,** was an Indian lawyer, activist, and politician who lived from 6 May 1861 to 6 February 1931. Also, he presided over Congress twice (1919–1920 and 1928–1929).
 
• **He was the ancestor of the Nehru-Gandhi dynasty** and the father of **India's first prime minister, Jawaharlal Nehru.**

questions.question: Who was the first to accurately describe the rings of Saturn as a disc around the planet in 1655?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Christiaan Huygens.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Humans have been fascinated by the **planet Saturn **for generations.
 
• **Christiaan Huygens, a Dutch astronomer, was the first to correctly characterise Saturn's rings **as a disc encircling the planet in 1655.
 
• **Galileo Galilei,** an Italian astronomer, had seen them when he first pointed his telescope towards Saturn in 1610, but his instrument was not strong enough to determine their real nature.
 
• Moreover, **Titan, Saturn's largest moon, was found by Huygens.**
 
• **Four of Saturn's moons were found by Italian astronomer Giovanni Cassini, **along with divisions inside the planet's rings.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Hideki Yukawa**

 
 
• ​In **Kyoto**, where he was raised alongside two older brothers, two older sisters, and two younger brothers, he was raised as **Hideki Ogawa**, his birth name.
 
• He eventually read **Lao Tzu and Chuang Tzu** after reading the **Confucian Doctrine of the Mean**. Due to the fact that he "was not as outstanding a student as his older brothers," his father briefly thought about sending him to technical college rather than university.
 
 
 
• **Galileo Galilei**
 
 
• ​**Galileo di Vincenzo Bonaiuti de' Galilei,** frequently referred to as a polymath, was an Italian astronomer, physicist, and engineer who lived from 15 February 1564 to 8 January 1642. Formally known as **Galileo.**
 
• He was born in Pisa, which at the time belonged to the **Duchy of Florence.**
 
 
 
• **Giovanni Cassini**
 
 
• **​Giovanni Domenico Cassini**, sometimes known as **Jean-Dominique Cassini,** was an Italian (naturalized French) mathematician, astronomer, and engineer who lived from 8 June 1625 to 14 September 1712.
 
• **Cassini** was born at **Perinaldo**, a town close to Imperia, in the **Savoyard **state's County of Nice at the time. 
 
 

a9:T

questions.question: October and November months in India comes under which among the following seasons?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Autumn.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ** Autumn's retreating/post-monsoon season** and the **transitional months of October and November c**oincide with the sun's passage southward. The low-pressure trough across the northern plains, known as the monsoon trough, weakens.

 
 
• High-pressure system gradually replaces this.
 
• The southwest monsoon winds begin to wane and ultimately wither away.
 
• The monsoon leaves the **Northern Plains at the start of October.**
 
• **Mid-November through mid-March is the period of time when it is cold.**
 
• **Mid-March through May is the hot weather season.**
 
• **June through September is the southwest monsoon season.**
 
• **Fall monsoons, from mid-October through mid-November.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• In **India, there are four distinct seasons:**

 
 
• Cold Weather Season (Winter) from December to February.
 
• Hot Weather Season (Summer) from March to May.
 
• South-West Monsoon Season (Rainy) from June to September.
 
• Season of Retreating Monsoon (Autumn) from October and November.

questions.question: Which of the following countries hosted the first edition of the Summer Youth Olympic Games in 2010?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Singapore__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The inaugural winter version took place in **Innsbruck**, **Austria** from 13 to 22 January 2012, while the **first summer version took place in Singapore from 14 to 26 August 2010**.
 
• **The International Olympic Committee (IOC)** organises the **Youth Olympic Games (YOG)**, an international multisport **competition for competitors between the ages of 15 and 18.**
 
• Similar to the present** Olympic Games** pattern, the games are held every four years and alternate between summer and winter competitions.
 
• However, the **Olympic Winter Games** are held in leap years rather than the summer competitions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Youth Olympic Games**

 
 
• **Johann Rosenzopf, an Austrian industrial manager, came up with the idea for the Youth Olympic Games in 1998.**
 
• This was in reaction to growing worries about juvenile obesity and a decline in kid engagement in sports, particularly among those in affluent countries, on a global scale.
 
• It was also acknowledged that a youth-focused** Olympics would encourage participation in the main event.**
 
• The **IOC's** response of conducting a strictly sporting event was unfavourable despite these arguments in favour of having an **Olympic event** for young people.

questions.question: The height of stumps in cricket is ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 28 inches.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The three vertical pillars that support the bails and create the wicket in cricket are known as the stumps.**
 
• A batsman might be dismissed by getting stumped or by being stumped oneself.
 
• Except for the bail grooves,** the tops of the stumps must be dome-shaped and 28 inches/71.12 **cm above the playing surface.
 
• Apart from the domed top, a stump's **uppermost** component must be **cylindrical** with a **circular section with a diameter of at least 1.38 in (3.50 cm) and no more than 1.5 in (3.81 cm).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information**__

**Stumps**

 
• 
 
 
• **Three vertical posts serve as the stumps and hold up two bails.** At each end of the pitch, a wicket is created by the combination of the stumps and bails, which are typically constructed of wood, most frequently ash.
 
• **Each stump is identified with a unique name:**
 
 
• **Off stump** is the stump that is on the other side of the wicket from the batsman.
 
• **The middle of the three stumps **is referred to as the middle stump.
 
• **Leg stump** is the stump that is on the same side as the batsman's legs as the wicket.

questions.question: Which of the following is a feature of Self-Help group?

options.text: The group takes care of the debt recovery.
There is a requirement of collateral.
These groups are classified as commercial banks.
The interest rates are generally high.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is the group takes care of the debt recovery.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The debt recovery is handled through the self-help organisation.**
 
• In the **area of employment and income-generating activities,** they work to increase the functional ability of the **underprivileged and marginalised groups in society.**
 
• They provide** collateral-free loans **to groups of people who typically struggle to obtain loans from banks.
 
• Also, they use group leadership and conversations to resolve disputes.
 
• They are a **crucial supplier of microfinance services **to the underprivileged.
 
• They serve as a conduit for official banking services to the underprivileged, particularly in rural areas.
 
• Also, they **urge the impoverished to develop a saving habit.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Self-Help Group** 

 
 
• The** Self-Employed Women's Association was founded in 1970**, marking the beginning of **SHG in India (SEWA).**
 
• The** SHG Bank Linkage Programme of NABARD, **which began in 1992, has expanded to become the largest microfinance programme in the world.
 
• Since 1993, **SHGs **have been able to open savings accounts with the **RBI and NABARD. The SHG-Bank **link programme was made possible thanks to this initiative, which also strengthened the **SHG movement.**
 
• **The Swarn Jayanti Gram Swarozgar Yojana (SGSY)**, launched by the Indian government in 1999, aims to encourage rural** SHG development and skill-based self-employment.**
 
• The programme was expanded into a statewide movement in 2011, leading to the creation of the **National Rural Livelihoods Mission (NRLM),** the greatest poverty reduction initiative in the history of the planet.

questions.question: Rukmani Devi Arundale was a famous dancer of which Indian classical dance form?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Bharatanatyam.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• An advocate for animal rights, as well as a **Bharatanatyam dancer and choreographer, Rukmini Devi Arundale, was an Indian theosophist.**
 
• **She was the first woman ever nominated to the Rajya Sabha, **which is the upper chamber of parliament for India.
 
• **She was the most renowned proponent of bringing back Bharatanatyam in its original "Sadhir" style,** which was beloved by Devadasi temple dancers, and she also worked to revive traditional Indian arts and crafts.
 
• One of **India Today's "100 Persons Who Shaped India" is Rukmini Devi.**
 
• She was awarded the **Padma Bhushan in 1956**, and the **Sangeet Natak Akademi Fellowship in 1967.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bharatanatyam**

 
 
• **​It is an important Hindu style of Indian classical dance.**
 
• The **Natya Shastra by Bharata Muni and the Abhinaya Darpana (Mirror of Gesture) by Nandikeshvara** are considered to be the **first sources of Bharatanatyam (an Indian classical dance form).**
 
• **The dance style is also briefly discussed in Manasollasa, a Kannada work by Someshwara III.**
 
• It has flourished in southern India's temples and courts since antiquity.
 
• It is one of eight well-known types of classical Indian dance that are influenced by **South Indian religions, primarily Shaivism, Vaishnavism, and Shaktism, which are referred to as Hinduism.**
